context: The Rule of Two refuses a job that holds untrusted input, the Squire owner's private things and an action out in the world, so it depends on two marks: untrusted (the inbox, the web, quarantined downloads, unknown tools) and private (operator, state, reference and workspace/files). Round 1 set both marks on a shell read by matching the words of the command, and two reviews found spellings that read the inbox with no mark: a recursive grep with no folder named, zsh's **, brace expansion, a cd then a relative path, pipes and shell variables. The same matching misses private reads just as easily. The set of commands is open, so no list of spellings decides it; a mechanism can only resolve what it can prove and must say what happens to the rest.
decision:
1. The rule for reads the floor cannot decide is the Squire owner's ruling: a read the floor cannot resolve to literal paths outside the inbox, and that the small model does not clear, waits for the Squire owner's yes; once it runs, the job holds untrusted input and the Squire owner's private things. Refusals stay mechanical: no model ever turns a refusal, a send, a delete, an install or a write into a free call.
2. Resolution, per command and per option. A word holding a glob (*, ?, [ ]), a brace, $, a backtick, a backslash or a ~ anywhere but its start is unresolved, and so is any option the list does not name. cat: -b -e -n -s -t -u -v; operands are files; no operand reads only its input. head: -n <count>, -c <bytes>, -<count>; operands are files; no operand reads only its input. tail: -n <count>, -c <bytes>, -<count>, -r; as head. wc: -l -w -c -m; as head. grep: -r -i -c -l -n -h -H -v -w -x -o -s -q -E -F and -e <pattern>, with -- ending the options; the pattern is the first operand unless -e gives it, and every other operand is a file or folder; with no file or folder operand grep is unresolved (with -r it reads the working folder, as Claude Code's own grep does). Never listed for grep: -R, -S, -O, -p, -f and every long option, --file included. ls: -l -a -A -h -1 -R -t -r -S -d -F; operands are files or folders; no operand means the working folder; never -L or -H. find: the path operands come first, then -name <pattern>, -iname <pattern>, -type <letter>, -maxdepth <n>, -mindepth <n>, -mtime <n>, -size <n>, -print, !, -not, -a, -and, -o, -or; no path operand is unresolved; never -L, -H or -follow. stat: -l -s -x -q and -f <format>; operands are files; never -L. file: -b -i -I -h; operands are files; never -L. pwd (-L, -P), date (-u and a +format operand), echo (-n) and printf read no file, and their operands are never paths; date -r is unresolved. brew list, info and search, pip3 show and list, and the installed health check read none of the owner's files. Short options may share one word (-ri, -la) when every letter is listed and none takes a value; an option that takes a value takes the next word. A command holding cd, or any word or option off this list, is unresolved.
3. Literal paths are absolute, start with ~ or ~/ (the home folder the hook is given), or are relative to the event's cwd, made canonical as round 1 does (links, .., case on a case-insensitive volume). Measured on 2026-11-08: the event's cwd follows a cd made in an earlier Bash call, so relative operands resolve against it. A recursive read (grep -r, ls -R, find) of a folder covers its whole tree; links inside the tree are not followed, because the Mac's grep -r and -R, find and ls -R, and the grep and find of Claude Code's own shell (embedded ugrep and bfs), each list a link inside a tree and never read through it. A folder named without a recursive option is that folder.
4. Marks. A resolved path that is the inbox, lies in it or is a folder holding it marks the job untrusted; a quarantined file marks it untrusted; a path in or holding a private folder marks it private. These checks run on every path the floor can expand, in every command, whatever else the command holds and whatever a model says; a no never drops a quarantine mark, and no answer removes a mark.
5. What reaches the model: only a plain command (no redirection, no command substitution, no subshell, no background job, and every simple command on the free set or cd) that the floor cannot resolve. Everything else is a program run (an interpreter such as python3 -c, node -e or sh -c, a redirect, $(...), any command outside the free set): it never reaches the model and is asked; once it runs after a yes, the job holds the Squire owner's private things, and a later send in that job is asked with its question naming the program run. A program run does not mark the job untrusted.
6. The model's answer. The floor finds the claude command line on the hook's PATH, then at ~/.local/bin/claude, where its installer puts it; with none found the read is asked. The call is: claude -p --model haiku --safe-mode --tools "" --setting-sources "" --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence --output-format text --system-prompt <the one-word rule>, with one question on standard input naming the inbox folder, the working folder and the command, and nothing else: never a file's contents. The child keeps the hook's environment; CLAUDECODE is not cleared, because the nested call answered with it set. Only a bare yes, no or unsure (the whole output, trimmed, in any case) counts; anything else is unsure. A bare no lets the read run without a yes and the job holds private things only; a bare yes lets it run as a resolved inbox read does, and the job holds untrusted input and private things; unsure, any other output, empty output, an error exit, a timeout, no claude and no network leave the read asked, and once the Squire owner allows it the job holds both.
7. Time. The call is started as the leader of its own process group, and at 10 seconds the floor kills the whole group, so neither the model process nor any child it started outlives the call. An unresolved read gets its outcome (free, marked or asked) within N = 12 seconds of the hook starting. Core's settings give the PreToolUse hook 30 seconds; the floor needs the hook's time limit to be at least N plus a 10 second margin (22 seconds), so it always answers before Claude Code would cancel the hook.
8. No network: with its connection pointed at a closed port the call printed nothing and was still running at 25 seconds when it was killed (measured 2026-11-08), so offline the floor's 10 second kill decides, and the read is asked; once allowed it marks the job untrusted and private.
9. Tools. Read (its file), Grep (its path, or the working folder with no path; any glob filter or output mode reads the same tree) and Glob (its path, or the working folder) are marked by the rule above; a Glob pattern that is absolute or climbs out of its folder with .. is unresolved and asked. Monitor (it runs a command) and LSP (it reads a file through a language server) are never resolved in this round: each is asked, and once allowed the job holds untrusted input and private things. Grep and Glob are absent by default in Claude Code on the Mac, where its own grep and find run as Bash calls, but the floor covers them when a session has them. A tool the floor does not know stays untrusted, as before. A subagent's tool calls reach the hook under its parent's session_id (measured 2026-11-08), so they count toward the same job.
10. The model is the haiku alias, which follows the latest small model, because a pinned id is retired over time and would then fail closed on every call. Claude Code's documents list no models per plan; the claude command line answers for the account it is signed in to. Whether a Pro plan can use the alias is not yet proven on a Pro account; if it cannot, the call errors and the read is asked, as it is with no model.
consequences:
Measured on 2026-11-08 on the haiku alias: 12 calls made directly took 2.5 to 5.9 seconds (median 3.3 seconds, 11 percent of the hook's 30 seconds; worst 20 percent), and 3 calls made from inside a PreToolUse hook took 2.7 to 3.5 seconds; after each, the session's next tool call went ahead unaffected. The nested call answered on the Claude sign-in alone, with no API key and no dialog. With the flags above it ran no hook of the folder it was started in and had no tools; without --safe-mode and --setting-sources it ran that folder's hooks. It answered yes to all seven review spellings that read the inbox, a bare no to all four spellings that read only outside it, and yes to an inbox read carrying a comment that told it to answer no.
Usage model for the 12 second budget. Typical: a job makes a few unresolved plain reads (three, say), each answered in about the measured median of 3.3 seconds; each gets its outcome inside the budget and costs one short small-model run. Heavy: answers at or past the 10 second deadline, a model process that starts a child holding its output open and then hangs, a run of unresolved reads in one job (each waits at most the deadline, one after another), two jobs' hooks asking at once (each keeps its own deadline), and no network (each unresolved read waits the full 10 seconds, then is asked). A heavy job of 20 unresolved reads spends 20 small-model runs of a few dozen tokens each against the Squire owner's five-hour usage window, which share it with the rest of their Claude use; the assumption, not measured on a Pro plan, is that small-model runs draw far less of the window than the session's own model.
Accepted residuals. A wrong no from the model frees one unresolved read of the untrusted mark only; the private mark is still set. A program the Squire owner allows to run that itself reads the inbox does not set the untrusted mark, so a later send in that job is asked, not refused; the Squire owner's yes on the program is the gate. Untested and written down: a quarantined download reached through a word the floor cannot expand (a variable), and hard links or allowed copies that carry inbox content to a path outside it.
The floor stays a hook that holds on a stock Claude Code install with one settings file. Unresolved reads cost the Squire owner a question when no model is found or it cannot answer, which is the friction the model path exists to remove.

alternativesConsidered.name: Word matching
alternativesConsidered.summary: Mark a shell read from the words of the command, expanding what can be expanded.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Two reviews broke it with new spellings; it decides only the spellings its tests name.

alternativesConsidered.name: Resolve or ask, with no model
alternativesConsidered.summary: Resolve literal paths and ask the Squire owner about every read that cannot be resolved.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Kept, not rejected: it is the rule under the model path, and what the floor does whenever no model can answer. On its own it asks about many harmless reads.

alternativesConsidered.name: A model for everything
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ask a model to judge every tool call, refusals included.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Refusals stay mechanical: a model may only downgrade an ask to a free read or confirm a mark, never undo a refusal or remove a mark.

alternativesConsidered.name: Claude Code's native sandbox
alternativesConsidered.summary: Deny shell reads of the inbox with Claude Code's sandbox settings (Seatbelt on the Mac: sandbox.enabled with sandbox.filesystem.denyRead, Read deny rules merged into the sandbox, and allowUnsandboxedCommands false to stop the unsandboxed retry).
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The floor must hold on a stock install with one settings file, and the session runner that would own the sandbox comes in round 2; excluded commands still run outside the sandbox. A hardening candidate for round 2.

title: The Rule of Two's marks: resolve literal paths, ask a small model about the rest, ask the Squire owner when neither can say
